acetaldehyde /ˌasəˈtaldəˌhīd/![What is Acetaldehyde and Do I Need To Worry About It? | by ...](data:image/webp;base64,)
**Acetaldehyde** (also called **ethanal** or **acetic aldehyde** , chemical formula C₂H₄O or CH₃CHO) is `a colorless, volatile organic compound with a pungent, fruity odor that occurs naturally in plants and forms in the body when alcohol is broken down`.[[1]](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6527032/)[[2]](https://www.powerthesaurus.org/acetylaldehyde/definitions)[[3]](https://www.naturalpedia.com/acetaldehyde-toxicity-side-effects-diseases-and-environmental-impacts.html)[[4]](https://www.dcceew.gov.au/environment/protection/npi/substances/acetaldehyde)

### Role in the Body and Alcohol Metabolism

- **Alcohol breakdown:** When you drink ethanol (alcohol), the liver enzyme alcohol dehydrogenase (ADH) converts it into acetaldehyde.[[1]](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6527032/)[[2]](https://www.ck12.org/flexi/life-science/digestive-system/-how-is-alcohol-broken-down-metabolized-and-removed-from-the-body/)
- **Further processing:** The enzyme aldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH) quickly converts acetaldehyde into acetate, which the body breaks down further into water and carbon dioxide.[[1]](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6527032/)[[2]](https://www.ck12.org/flexi/life-science/digestive-system/-how-is-alcohol-broken-down-metabolized-and-removed-from-the-body/)
- **Health effects:** Acetaldehyde is toxic and irritating. Short-term exposure or buildup can irritate the eyes, skin, and respiratory tract, and is associated with unpleasant hangover symptoms. Long-term or high exposure is linked to serious health risks, including DNA damage and cancer.[[1]](https://www.epa.gov/sites/default/files/2016-09/documents/acetaldehyde.pdf)[[2]](https://www.drinkwel.com/blogs/drinkwel-blog/24806145-alcohol-chemistry-101-understanding-acetaldehyde-and-glutathione)[[3]](https://enjoyupside.com/blogs/blog/acetaldehyde-toxicity-symptoms)

### Natural Occurrence and Brewing

- **Nature and food:** It appears naturally in ripening fruits (such as apples), plant respiration, sugar metabolism, and fermented foods like yogurt, bread, and vinegar.[[1]](https://www.dcceew.gov.au/environment/protection/npi/substances/acetaldehyde)[[2]](https://www.naturalpedia.com/acetaldehyde-toxicity-side-effects-diseases-and-environmental-impacts.html)
- **Brewing and winemaking:** It is a normal intermediate of yeast fermentation. As [Tastings](https://www.tastings.com/Drinkipedia/Acetaldehyde-Definition.aspx) notes, excess acetaldehyde can act as a fermentation flaw in beer, wine, or cider—creating aromas or flavors of green or sour apple, cut grass, or latex—often linked to under-active yeast, pulling yeast too early, or low fermentation temperatures.[[1]](https://www.dcceew.gov.au/environment/protection/npi/substances/acetaldehyde)[[2]](https://www.tastings.com/Drinkipedia/Acetaldehyde-Definition.aspx)

### Industrial and Chemical Uses

- **Properties:** It boils near room temperature at 20.2 °C (68.36 °F) and melts at -123.4 °C (-190.1 °F), existing as a liquid or gas depending on conditions.
- **Applications:** It is used in organic synthesis and biochemical research, and serves as an important industrial aldehyde intermediate.[[1]](https://www.powerthesaurus.org/acetylaldehyde/definitions)

Acetaldehyde (CH 3 CHO CH sub 3 CHO C H 3 C H O ) is `a highly reactive, colorless, and flammable liquid or gas with a pungent, fruity odor` . It is a major industrial chemical, a natural component in coffee and ripe fruit, and a toxic byproduct of alcohol metabolism, contributing to hangovers, nausea, and headaches.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acetaldehyde)[[2]](https://zbiotics.com/blogs/journal/what-is-acetaldehyde-and-its-link-to-alcohol)[[3]](https://brewingscience.com/acetaldehyde-in-beer-understanding-its-role-and-how-to-minimize-it/)[[4]](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/qqsNrI7Lj-4#:~:text=Unfinished%20beer%20is%20a%20term%20commonly%20used,aromas%20of%20green%20apples%20or%20pumpkin%20rind.)

**Key Aspects of Acetaldehyde:** 

- **Alcohol Metabolism:** The liver breaks down alcohol into acetaldehyde, which is further metabolized by the enzyme aldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH) into non-toxic acetate. A buildup of this toxic, intermediate compound causes alcohol-induced damage and hangover symptoms.
- **Health Hazards:** It is classified as a probable human carcinogen (Group 1). Exposure can cause skin, eye, and respiratory irritation, and chronic exposure may lead to issues similar to alcohol-related diseases.
- **Sources & Uses:** It is used to produce perfumes, polyester resins, dyes, and as a flavoring agent. It is found in tobacco smoke, automobile exhaust, and as a byproduct of fermentation (e.g., in unfinished beer).
- **Chemical Properties:** It is highly flammable and acts as a key intermediate in the synthesis of other chemical compounds.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acetaldehyde)[[2]](https://zbiotics.com/blogs/journal/what-is-acetaldehyde-and-its-link-to-alcohol)[[3]](https://brewingscience.com/acetaldehyde-in-beer-understanding-its-role-and-how-to-minimize-it/)[[4]](https://www.epa.gov/sites/default/files/2016-09/documents/acetaldehyde.pdf)[[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/medicine-and-dentistry/acetaldehyde)[[6]](https://dhss.delaware.gov/wp-content/uploads/sites/10/dph/pdf/Acetaldehyde_FAQ_PUB_ENG_0323.pdf)[[7]](https://www.rivm.nl/en/tobacco/harmful-substances-in-tobacco-smoke/acetaldehyde#:~:text=Acetaldehyde%20has%20many%20uses%2C%20including:%20*%20**Production,an%20average%20of%201%20microgram%20of%20acetaldehyde.)[[8]](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/qqsNrI7Lj-4#:~:text=Unfinished%20beer%20is%20a%20term%20commonly%20used,aromas%20of%20green%20apples%20or%20pumpkin%20rind.)

It is found everywhere, including in the air, food, and water.[[1]](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK498781/)[[2]](https://www.dcceew.gov.au/environment/protection/npi/substances/fact-sheets/acetaldehyde#:~:text=Acetaldehyde%20can%20be%20emitted%20from%20cooking%20hamburgers%2C,the%20evaporation%20of%20acetaldehyde%20from%20certain%20foods.)[[3]](https://www.epa.gov/sites/default/files/2016-09/documents/acetaldehyde.pdf)

items.markdown:
![Acetaldehyde – C 2 H 4 O](https://api.dataforseo.com/cdn/i/05161028-1087-0066-0000-eb1824c87673:4)
Acetaldehyde is `a highly reactive, naturally occurring organic chemical compound` (C H 3 C H O cap C cap H sub 3 cap C cap H cap O𝐶𝐻3𝐶𝐻𝑂). It is primarily known as a toxic byproduct of alcohol metabolism in the human body and a key intermediate in industrial manufacturing.[](https://zbiotics.com/blogs/journal/what-is-acetaldehyde-and-its-link-to-alcohol) [[1]](https://zbiotics.com/blogs/journal/what-is-acetaldehyde-and-its-link-to-alcohol)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acetaldehyde)[[3]](https://www.britannica.com/science/acetaldehyde)

How it is Formed

- **In the body:** When you consume alcohol, your liver breaks down ethanol, creating acetaldehyde as the very first step. It is highly toxic before the body further converts it into harmless acetate.
- **In food and nature:** It occurs naturally in ripe fruits, coffee, bread, and is a byproduct of yeast fermentation (giving unfinished beer a "green apple" flavor).
- **In tobacco and environment:** It is a major component of tobacco smoke and is found in vehicle exhaust.[](https://zbiotics.com/blogs/journal/what-is-acetaldehyde-and-its-link-to-alcohol) [[1]](https://zbiotics.com/blogs/journal/what-is-acetaldehyde-and-its-link-to-alcohol)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acetaldehyde)[[3]](https://www.beerandbrewing.com/dictionary/3VI3x2O47b)[[4]](https://brewingscience.com/acetaldehyde-in-beer-understanding-its-role-and-how-to-minimize-it/)[[5]](https://fragranceconservatory.com/ingredient/acetaldehyde)[[6]](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/Acetaldehyde)[[7]](https://oehha.ca.gov/air/chemicals/acetaldehyde)

Physical Properties

- **Appearance:** A colorless, volatile liquid or gas.
- **Odor:** Has a pungent, suffocating smell, though at very dilute concentrations it smells fruity and pleasant.
- **Reactivity:** It is highly flammable and reactive.[](https://zbiotics.com/blogs/journal/what-is-acetaldehyde-and-its-link-to-alcohol) [[1]](https://zbiotics.com/blogs/journal/what-is-acetaldehyde-and-its-link-to-alcohol)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acetaldehyde)[[3]](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK208113/)[[4]](https://www.epa.gov/sites/default/files/2016-09/documents/acetaldehyde.pdf)[[5]](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK219914/)

Health and Toxicity

- **The Hangover Effect:** Acetaldehyde buildup is a primary cause of alcohol hangover symptoms, including nausea, headaches, and a racing heart.
- **Alcohol Flush:** People with a common genetic variant (especially those of East Asian descent) lack the enzyme to properly break down acetaldehyde, causing their face to flush red and resulting in rapid discomfort when drinking alcohol.
- **Cancer Risk:** The International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) classifies acetaldehyde as a Group 1 human carcinogen, meaning it has the potential to damage DNA and increase cancer risks.[](https://zbiotics.com/blogs/journal/what-is-acetaldehyde-and-its-link-to-alcohol) [[1]](https://zbiotics.com/blogs/journal/what-is-acetaldehyde-and-its-link-to-alcohol)[[2]](https://www.beerandbrewing.com/dictionary/3VI3x2O47b)[[3]](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/Acetaldehyde)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acetaldehyde)[[5]](https://www.epa.gov/sites/default/files/2016-09/documents/acetaldehyde.pdf)

Industrial Uses Despite its toxicity, it is a crucial chemical used as a starting material to manufacture:[[1]](https://www.britannica.com/science/acetaldehyde)

- Plastics and synthetic rubber
- Perfumes, dyes, and flavorings
- Acetic acid and ethyl acetate[](https://www.britannica.com/science/acetaldehyde) [[1]](https://www.britannica.com/science/acetaldehyde)[[2]](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/Acetaldehyde)
